questions.prompt: Which of these is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: A vector has both size and direction.

questions.prompt: You walk 6 km east and then 8 km north. What is the size of your displacement?
A runner completes one lap of a 400 m track. What are the distance and displacement?
Adam walks 700 m to school in 560 s. What is his average speed?
Can an object have zero displacement after moving a large distance?
options: Only if it moves very slowly
Only if it moves in a straight line
Yes, if it returns to its starting point
questions.explain: Displacement only compares start and finish positions.

questions.prompt: Adam cycles 3 km to school in 12 minutes and back home in 15 minutes. What is his average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
questions.explain: Total distance 6 km in 27 min = 0.45 h; 6 ÷ 0.45 ≈ 13.33 km/h.

questions.prompt: What is his average velocity for that whole round trip?
questions.explain: He ends at home, so his displacement, and therefore his average velocity, is zero.

questions.prompt: Plan a simple investigation to measure your average walking speed and velocity between your classroom and the school gate.
questions.modelAnswer: Measure the path length with a measuring tape or trundle wheel (distance), and the straight-line distance and direction from classroom to gate from a map (displacement). Time the walk with a stopwatch several times and take the mean time. Average speed = distance ÷ time; average velocity = displacement ÷ time, in the direction of the gate. Keep the route and walking pace the same each trial.
